subject: CloudCare DPA counter-redlines: technical evidence binder & escalation path
messages:
From: Claire Wong <claire@cloudcare.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>; Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>; Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal Ops <legal@cloudcare.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Sep 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: CloudCare DPA counter-redlines and SCCs questions

Hi Marissa / team,

Thanks for sending the draft MSA + Order Form. Our legal team has returned a DPA counter-redline (attached) with three high-priority asks that will determine whether we can proceed on the timeline:

1) SCCs: they want to adopt the new EU SCCs and have two unusual deletions in the Annex that remove our proposed subprocessors clause. They request a separate "transfer impact addendum" that documents routing and safeguards.
2) KMS / Key custody: they want an option to hold a customer-managed envelope key and need specifics on how KMS rotation would work.
3) Evidence & jurisdiction mapping: Procurement asked for a packaged "technical evidence binder" (diagram of data flows by region, list of sub-processors, retention windows, and PII classification) to accompany the DPA.

Can we get a 1–2 page summary from Redwood that:
- Confirms which SCC Annexes will be signed (and whether any clauses will be negotiated)
- Outlines the KMS options / controls and the timeline to support a customer-managed key
- Provides a preliminary evidence bundle (or a single link to a binder) we can include with our legal submission

We attach: cloudcare-dpa-counter-redlines.docx (their redline). Hoping to agree next steps quickly — are you available for a 30-minute sync tomorrow (Fri) or Monday?

Best,
Claire
Claire Wong
Head of Legal Operations, CloudCare

Attachments: cloudcare-dpa-counter-redlines.docx (docx)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Claire Wong <claire@cloudcare.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Sep 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CloudCare DPA counter-redlines and SCCs questions

Hi Claire — thanks for the clear list and for the redline. We reviewed the attachment and have split this into two tracks internally: legal commercial redlines (SCCs / Annex edits) and technical evidence / ops questions (KMS, subprocessor mapping, data flows).

Quick answers up front:
- SCCs: Redwood is prepared to sign the new EU SCCs; the parts CloudCare flagged that touch subprocessors are negotiable but we need to preserve our right to use vetted cloud providers.
- KMS: we support a customer-managed envelope key option. There is an onboarding path but it requires a short (2–3 week) technical enablement and a review of certificate exchange.
- Evidence binder: we can produce an initial package (diagram + subprocessor list + retention matrix) by EOD Monday if that works for your legal team.

I propose a 30-minute call Monday 09/17 at 9:00am PT to walk through both tracks and confirm whether anything requires an escalation to Legal Ops. Karthik, can you prepare the technical checklist (KMS runbook + rotation schedule + any constraints around on-prem storage) before Monday? Ben/Laura — please flag any commercial points that need escalation.

Thanks — talk Monday if that works.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-dpa-initial-checklist.xlsx (internal)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Claire Wong <claire@cloudcare.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Sep 2028 16:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CloudCare DPA counter-redlines and SCCs questions

On Thu, Sep 14, 2028 at 08:12 Claire Wong <claire@cloudcare.com> wrote:
> Thanks for sending the draft MSA + Order Form. Our legal team has returned a DPA counter-redline (attached) with three high-priority asks that will determine whether we can proceed on the timeline:

Thanks — quick technical notes below (I can present these on Monday):

1) KMS / Customer-managed key (CMK):
- We support CMK using envelope encryption. Customer provides public key material and we wrap the DEK. Rotation: Redwood supports quarterly rotations; a one-time key-swap is available during onboarding.
- Limitation: historical tokens stored in Redwood may remain encrypted under prior DEKs until re-encryption is scheduled (we provide a rewrap utility but it’s an offline migration that adds time).

2) Subprocessors & evidence binder:
- We can provide a downloadable binder (zipped) that contains: subprocessor list, SOC2 scoping statement for infra providers, region-by-region dataflow diagrams (PNG), and retention matrix (CSV). I linked a working folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdExampleEvidenceBinder

3) Transfer impact addendum (TIA):
- If CloudCare insists on a formal TIA, we can supply a templated addendum that enumerates routing (EU -> EU only by default), fallback to US when authorized, and technical mitigations (encryption, access controls, logging).

Open item for legal: whether Redwood's vetted subprocessors clause must remain verbatim or can be converted to an approval list for this customer. That decision drives operational work for the binder.

I will attach the proposed KMS rotation schedule and a short tech note on rewrap that covers migration effort.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Infrastructure Security, Redwood Inference

Attachments: kms-rotation-schedule.xlsx (xlsx), tech-note-rewrap.txt (txt)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Claire Wong <claire@cloudcare.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Sep 2028 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CloudCare DPA counter-redlines and SCCs questions

Marissa / Claire —

Thanks for the quick coordination. From a commercial/procurement angle:
- If CloudCare requires an explicit TIA and removal of our standard subprocessors clause, this will likely trigger an approval path up to VP Legal and may add 2–3 weeks to contracting. Please confirm whether CloudCare can accept a scoped exception (i.e., an explicit subprocessor approval list for the account) instead of a full deletion.
- I pulled together inline commercial suggestions and a short redline PDF attached — they preserve SCC adoption while attempting to avoid deletion of the subprocessors clause.

Next steps proposed:
1) Redwood provides Monday EOD a preliminary evidence binder (per Karthik).
2) CloudCare legal confirms which approach they prefer on subprocessors (delete vs account-specific approval).
3) If CloudCare insists on full deletion, Laura and I will escalate to Legal Ops (we'll need to loop in Contracts and Product Security).

Attaching: redline-suggestions.pdf (PDF)

Cheers,
Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Contracts & Legal Ops, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redline-suggestions.pdf (pdf)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: Sun, 16 Sep 2028 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CloudCare DPA counter-redlines and SCCs questions

Claire — thanks for the conversation this morning. Summary & owners below so nothing falls through the cracks: 

Summary of deliverables (owners / deadlines):
- Evidence binder (diagram, subprocessor list, retention matrix): Karthik — deliverable ready for shared link by 2028-09-18 EOD. (Will include initial SOC2 scoping excerpt.)
- KMS onboarding + rotation schedule + migration note: Karthik — provide the schedule spreadsheet (attached earlier) and a short step-by-step migration note by 2028-09-18.
- Commercial redline suggestions to try to preserve subprocessors clause: Ben & Laura — prepare final suggested language and escalation memo by 2028-09-19.
- Redwood to confirm acceptance of new EU SCCs in principle (legal): Marissa — will confirm by 2028-09-19 and escalate to Legal Ops if necessary.

If CloudCare needs an accelerated path (i.e., legal must sign the DPA this week), flag immediately — Ben/Laura and I will open an escalation ticket with Legal Ops and Product Security. Otherwise, we'll proceed on the dates above and deliver the binder by Monday.

One note for procurement: the CMK path is supported but has operational constraints (re-encryption of historical data is a migration project). We'll surface that explicitly in the binder so there are no surprises.

Thanks all — I will follow up with the shared Drive link once the binder is staged.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachments: technical-evidence-binder.zip (zip)
